Build a level-of-detail pyramid as an Arrow table

Source: R/pyramid.R
a5_pyramid_arrow.Rd

Builds the pyramid of a5_pyramid() and tiles it as a5_write_pyramid() does, but returns the tiles in memory as an Arrow Table instead of writing a file: the layout of the Parquet file, in Arrow. Use it where a file is not wanted, such as a viewer that ships the tiles to a browser itself, or to hand the pyramid to other Arrow tools.

Usage

a5_pyramid_arrow(
  x,
  ...,
  lods = NULL,
  aggregate = c("mean", "rep_child"),
  reducers = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  tile_size = 4096L,
  metadata = NULL,
  threads = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame with one a5R::a5_cell column, or an a5R::a5_cell vector. The cells must share one resolution and appear once each; rows with NA cells are dropped. An a5R::a5_covering holds cells at mixed resolutions: convert it with a5R::a5_uncompact() first.

...

<tidy-select> Value columns to carry into the pyramid. Default: every numeric column other than the cells.

lods

Integer vector of the coarser LODs to build, each below the leaves' resolution; the leaves are always kept. Default: every resolution from 2 up to the leaves'. Resolutions 0 and 1 hold the 12 and 60 largest cells, which no map view draws.

aggregate

The reducer for every value column: "mean" (default) or "rep_child". See "Reducers".

reducers

Named character vector of reducers for single columns, overriding aggregate, such as c(count = "sum", class = "mode").

weights

Name of a numeric column of non-negative leaf weights for "mean", "mode" and "rep_child", such as the npix column from a5px::a5_read_raster(). NA weights count as 0, and leaves with weight 0 do not count. Default NULL: every leaf counts once.

types

Named character vector of storage types for single columns, such as c(red = "uint8", ndvi = "float32"). See "Column types".

tile_size

The most rows in a tile (row group). Larger tiles mean fewer requests and a smaller footer; smaller tiles mean less data fetched outside the view. Default: 4096.

metadata

Named character vector or list of strings to add to the file's key-value metadata, such as a renderer's settings as JSON. The keys "a5pyramid", "a5_index" and "ARROW:schema" are reserved.

threads

Number of threads, or NULL (default) for a5pyramid_threads().

Value

An Arrow Table with one record batch per tile.

Details

Each record batch of the table is one tile, in the order of the file's row groups: arrow::as_record_batch_reader(tbl)$batches()[[i]] holds the rows of row group i - 1 of the same pyramid written with a5_write_pyramid(), and the table's schema metadata holds the same entries as the file's key-value metadata: the index under "a5pyramid", whose tiles and tile_bbox count record batches here as they count row groups in the file, the A5 index version under "a5_index", and metadata. The columns and their types are those of the file (see a5_write_pyramid()); a5R::a5_from_arrow_table() converts the table to a data frame with an a5R::a5_cell column.

The tiles cross from Rust through the Arrow C stream interface, so no value is copied through R. arrow::write_parquet(), arrow::write_feather() or arrow::write_to_raw() serialise the table, but only a5_write_pyramid() writes the encodings and statistics the file format specifies.

See also

a5_write_pyramid() for the same tiles in a Parquet file.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
x <- data.frame(cell = cells, value = runif(length(cells)))

tbl <- a5_pyramid_arrow(x, types = c(value = "float32"), tile_size = 500)
tbl
#> Table
#> 1426 rows x 4 columns
#> $cell <uint64 not null>
#> $lod <uint8 not null>
#> $ncell <uint32 not null>
#> $value <float>
#> 
#> See $metadata for additional Schema metadata
tiles <- arrow::as_record_batch_reader(tbl)$batches()
length(tiles)
#> [1] 17
index <- tbl$metadata$a5pyramid

a5_from_arrow_table(tbl)
